checks.label: Normal forwarding, rewrite, business errors and redirects preserve the upstream response
Connection refusal and pre-header disconnect are bounded 502 with a single final result
Response-header deadline applies with and without breakers; TLS setup is also bounded
Partial body stall aborts the original response; no replacement status or appended JSON
Continuous body progress cannot bypass total processing budget
Persistent failures open only their breaker; open admission never contacts upstream
Half-open probes have two permits; successful probes close, failed probes reopen
Already admitted requests finish independently after the breaker opens
Explicit same breaker names share local state
Write processed but response lost is sent once, without automatic retry
Client cancellation propagates, releases work, and is neither success nor breaker failure
Cancellation after response headers preserves the committed status and cancels the body
Pool queue is bounded and cancelled waiters/requests release connections
Gateway limiting and management authentication never increment upstream breaker failures

checks.label: Management authentication, authoritative preview and exact source-only rollback payload
Full rollback propagates automatically to B and restores real proxy limiting behavior; business requests add zero config reads
Two real instances retry the same recovery concurrently: one increment, one history fact and one original receipt
A normal commit racing B rollback on the same reviewed version produces one success and one recorded conflict
Same ID with changed source, type or expectedVersion fails while the original recovery remains unchanged
Redis execution blocked before SET: query stays unknown; a deliberate identical retry uses the original identity
Redis executed rollback but acknowledgement was lost: another instance confirms the original source and success
Actual browser: history selection, complete differences, real version conflict, explicit new operation and successful recovery
Real HTTP rollback response lost: auth recovery retains identity; querying historical success cannot regress current baseline or auto-submit
Actual in-flight history and preview responses become inert after explicit discard; cancel leave and new drafts remain protected
Previewed source cropped before confirmation is rejected, but prior successful recovery remains confirmed
Restart restores the latest snapshot and keeps historical rollback receipts queryable across instances

checks: Two independent processes restore one snapshot and expose authenticated local sync diagnostics
A committed update automatically changes B real proxy behavior from 200 to 429
Repeated confirmation refreshes check time without changing the actual adoption timestamp
Proxy requests and diagnostic reads add zero runtime Redis commands while one periodic read is held
Only B is disconnected; it retains its snapshot, exposes failure then expiry, and automatically recovers
A captured old read arriving after a newer B commit cannot roll back B or its adoption time
Consecutive update waves only publish complete ledger snapshots and never move the local revision backwards
Missing, corrupt, foreign-generation and same-version conflicting data are exposed without repair or publication
Restart restores the newest stored snapshot with a new instance identity and resumes automatic polling
Shutdown cancels an active sync read and releases all B proxy and named Redis connections

checks.label: Schema-1 migration preserves six fields and version; old HTTP writers fail closed
In-flight or absent operation is UNKNOWN, never not-executed; bounded transport failure preserves that fact
Two real instances submit the same ID and request concurrently: one increment, one receipt, identical original outcome
Same ID with changed values OR expectedVersion is rejected without changing configuration or original receipt
Later commits remain intact when another instance queries and retries an earlier successful operation
A recorded version conflict is a definite rejection and its replay cannot turn into a new write
Redis executed SET but its reply is lost: cross-instance receipt proves the original success even after another commit
Gateway restart keeps cross-instance receipts and duplicate submission returns the original receiving instance
Errors before the sole SET leave both configuration and receipts unchanged; multi-command Lua has no rollback
History has stable keyset pagination under new commits and count trimming does not remove promised receipts
Receipt expiry, seven-day history expiry, capacity admission and cleanup remain bounded without sleeping
Actual browser: lost HTTP response, auth expiry, query old success, preserved draft and explicit conflict resubmission

checks: Legacy six-field and schema-1 concurrent init preserve one version and six values; running reads never migrate
Actual previous Lua script refuses schema 3 in read/write/init without overwriting receipts
Backup retains exact receipts; all schema-3 rollback/recovery paths require explicit receipt-loss acknowledgement
Explicit format rollback produces a fresh schema-1 epoch; forward migration has no invented old receipts
Disaster recovery from schema-3 backup creates a new epoch and accurately loses old receipt availability

checks: A real conflict retains draft rate 40 and displays window 10 to 30
Repeated same-version reads preserve 10 to 30 and never resend the draft
A later update still compares from 10 while adopting the newest CAS version and untouched capacity
Unavailable reads and authentication recovery preserve comparison and draft without automatic writes
Manual review and save submit the latest version once and preserve all other writers values
A subsequent conflict and discarded draft start and clear the comparison at the correct boundaries
Legacy six-field JSON migrates on startup; GET and adopted expose one version and no-store
Missing versions and invalid fields are definitively rejected without storage changes
A window=30 succeeds; stale B rate=40 conflicts and cannot restore window=10
Twelve independent same-version HTTP writers released by one gate produce exactly one commit
Concurrent API reads match complete snapshots in the real storage commit ledger
Redis ACL rejection proves not-written and leaves both stored and local snapshots unchanged
Redis before-execution reply fault is conservative; explicit storage read converges
Redis after-execution reply fault is conservative; explicit storage read converges
A current storage read after a lost acknowledgement can see a later writer, without attributing the original request
Concurrent missing-key initialization and legacy migration have one winner without overwriting values
Invalid legacy/schema/types/ranges and exhausted revisions are rejected unchanged
Online key loss never silently initializes and a new generation cannot replace a running local snapshot
A restarted gateway restores exactly the stored version and all six values
Browser stale form preserves its draft and requires explicit conflict review before the second PUT
HTTP success response loss preserves uncertainty through failed reads and reconciles without another PUT
Browser confirmation sees another real writer and requires fresh review while preserving the intended edit
Authentication expiry and rejected navigation retain the draft; reconnection reads and requires review
Overview and route navigation retain authentication; proxy traffic performs no runtime-config Redis reads
Warm management-operation costs are recorded separately from the proxy hot path
Malformed persisted configuration refuses restart without overwriting storage or becoming ready
Desktop first viewport exposes all six parameters, exact units, baseline and disabled no-change save
Changed fields alone form current-to-draft comparisons; raw invalid values stay visible and block saving
Saving freezes edits and repeat submissions; confirmed values become the baseline
First loading and failed reads expose no defaults; a local retry establishes the baseline
Explicit save rejection preserves editable differences and a subsequent save can succeed
A lost response requires a read first; matching server values reconcile without another write
A confirmed save survives a later read failure and its independent retry
Disabled limiting retains its values; impossible bucket combinations explain behavior without inventing validation
Mobile and narrow layouts retain readable fields, summaries and all navigation destinations
Unsaved preview navigation and browser unloading are guarded; confirmed discard exits normally
Formal management authentication and initial source failure preserve an unknown baseline until retry
Formal PUT sends six fields, expectedVersion and operationId once and validates its receipt without another GET
Formal refresh retains edited fields while updating untouched server values
Formal rejected saves retain draft and inline server errors; network and 500 failures require reconciliation
Expired credentials preserve the draft in memory and re-authentication reads before enabling a save
Formal navigation, including trailing-slash settings URLs, and disconnect protect drafts; confirmed discard clears retained state
Authenticated backup preserves exact raw bytes and refuses overwriting an existing backup
Downgrade refuses to overwrite values changed since the backup
Offline downgrade leaves exactly the old six-field JSON
Restore creates a new generation with the backed-up six values, invalidating stale clients
Tampered backups cannot be restored
Missing-key recovery uses an atomic absence check and starts a fresh generation
Lua increments the last safe decimal revision exactly once and refuses overflow
A wrong Redis key type is rejected without deleting or replacing evidence
Normal route exposes actual ordered stages and conditional 429/503 branches
Node expands in place, exposes complete rewrite example and fields, Escape restores focus
Route switching removes unsupported stages and closes prior node panel
Search and filters keep current route until explicit selection; locate restores its directory page
32 routes paginate 6 per page, keep selection while browsing, and support keyboard selection across pages
Long route fields are complete, selectable and copyable as text and JSON
Configuration error is centralized, cached canvas remains, writes block, details and retry work
Preview create/edit/delete retains validation and generated-rule examples without live writes
320–1440px layouts keep long names readable and directory responsive at 6/4/2 entries
Mobile paging keeps the selected route; selection and node expansion fold the directory
Scenario tabs switch fixtures, and clicking the current tab preserves selection
Motion represents selection/expansion and honors reduced-motion preference
Normal, exception and 32-route browser screenshots fit a 1440×900 first viewport
Preview produces no JavaScript errors and makes no backend API requests
Real authentication and delayed initial loading: no fake route, empty-state action or demo controls
Initial route-read failure is distinct from a confirmed empty directory and recovers
UI create uses server validation, persists to Redis and forwards a real rewritten request
Editing updates forwarding, ordinary HTTP 500 passes through, and connection failure is classified as 502
Runtime polling updates the actual token-bucket stage and conditional branch
Failed refresh keeps actual cached route and blocks writes, then retry restores editing
Successful create followed by failed list refresh retains previous selection and reports both outcomes
Unavailable runtime/metrics/audit never appear healthy or as zero, and refresh recovers them
Disabled monitoring and latency overflow retain existing business semantics
Live navigation, narrow layout and copied fields remain connected to actual routes
Confirmed live deletion removes persisted and runtime routes; refresh failure is reported without losing context
Disconnect cancels polling; expired credentials return to login; preview remains isolated

limits: No automatic retry; timeouts/cancellation do not undo upstream side effects
Ordinary HTTP budget also applies to proxied streams; local monitoring SSE excluded
Breaker state is per process; explicit same names share it
Pool bounds are per upstream origin; breaker names remain until restart
No HTTP/2, WebSocket, gRPC, SYN-drop or TLS certificate-matrix end-to-end claim
Reactor body-cancellation signal and committed status describe observed gateway behavior, not end-client delivery acknowledgement
Latency bounds measured on this local isolated environment, not a production SLO
